title: Cavalier
summary: Cavalier is a powerful armored Titan who belonged to Sir Lancelot. A fighter, through and through, his armor is enchanted, his blades burn eternally, and his passion for battle is unmatched.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
Cavalier was amongst the strongest Titans in Medieval England and would only bond with noble, worthy, loyal men. Belonging to the Casterwill family for generations, he was used by Sir Lancelot, head of one of the main branch families. As the noblest of all King Arthur's knights, Cavalier took on aspects of his Seeker, most notably his pure heart. Eventually, Lancelot hid Cavalier's Amulet in Paris, France in his Mausoleum along with his secret books and scrolls. [Memory Lane]

Both the Huntik Foundation and the Organization became aware of Cavalier's Amulet and went to the Mausoleum recover it. After overcoming many traps and obstacles, Lok Lambert and Dante Vale reached the room where Cavalier's Amulet kept along with numerous ancient Casterwill tomes. However they were ambushed by Rassimov who went and reached the Amulet. Despite summoning the Titan, the worthy Titan refused to bond with Rassimov who declared that if he could not have the power then no one would. Rassimov then used Darkvoid to callously destroy Cavalier along with the entirety of Lancelot's books and scrolls. [Memory Lane] 

Sophie later studied Cavalier on the Cypherdex and deduced that it was no surprise that Cavalier would not bond with an evil man like Rassimov, while Dante hauntingly confirmed to Guggenheim that, without a doubt, Cavalier had been destroyed by Rassimov's devastating power. [Memory Lane]

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.wikitext:
Cavalier has the ability of flight and can use flaming swords in battle. As a powerful brawler Titan with a noble heart, Cavalier only bonds with a worthy and pure hearted Seeker and fiercely resits evil. His fighting prowess and victories are legendary among [[Seekers]].

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.wikitext:
* Cavalier's summoning command is "'''Your speed and might are mine to command, valiant warrior. Come forth, Cavalier'''."

* Cavalier's name is derived from the French word for knight, which is fitting since [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancelot Sir Lancelot] of the Lake was one of the Knights of the Round Table. Appropriately, some of the oldest mentions of Sir Lancelot in Arthurian legend were from France.
